alignments.note: Dative noun with its English case preposition; no article stands, so with rides with the noun (rule 21's determinerless clause). Discontinuous around many under rule 15. Head on honors.
Participle expanded into a finite clause; the supplied when and the subject we are its helpers (rules 7, 86). Head on sailed.

Compound ἐπιτίθημι rendered by the phrasal put on board; the particle on realizes the preverb and the supplied board completes the verb's own English, both riding inside the unit (rules 7, 106). Head on the verb word put.

Substantival article whose modifier is a prepositional phrase carrying no verb of its own, so the article keeps the supplied determiner-correlative such … as along with its nominal things, headed on the nominal (rules 22, 31). Giving as to πρός instead remains defensible.
The ASV absorbs πρός into the supplied predicate we needed and writes no word answering to it, which is the one case rule 36 allows a preposition to stand empty.
The ASV gives the recast noun no determiner, so the article realizes nothing (rule 23).
χρείας recast as the finite we needed; the supplied subject rides with it (rule 7). Head on needed.

review_notes: The variant unit is underdetermined on the base reading and every projected token is accounted for.
The placement of as is the contested point; the note in the article's unit records the alternative.
